items.title: CPI(M) leader P. Rajeeve flays police action against protesters in Keralam’s Thiruvananthapuram
points: Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] central committee member P.

Rajeeve has termed Wednesday night’s police action against protesters in Thiruvananthapuram and the removal to hospital of Valarmathi S., secretary of the action council and convener of the lower primary school teacher (LPST) rank holders’ protest…
The government must specify which court order within six months of the United Democratic Front (UDF) assuming power that it relied on for such actions.
Moreover, it owes an explanation on why it “went back” on an earlier assurance to extend the time frame for Public Service Commission rank lists.
Agitations are being “suppressed”, while social media accounts are being closed down, he told the media here on Thursday.
Likewise, the government that is finding fault with the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB) is taking credit for projects that were taken up under it.

items.title: 4 Food Stalls Destroyed In Fire At Shillong Literary Fest Venue
points: Four food stalls were destroyed in a fire at the Ward's Lake venue of the Shillong Literary Fest 2026 on Thursday evening.
The incident occurred around 8:30 pm, shortly after a talk show had concluded.
A musical programme was still underway at the venue, but the organisers were forced to halt it due to the fire.
The temporary structures erected at the venue were engulfed in flames within minutes before the blaze could be brought under control.
Four stalls were destroyed in the fire, East Khasi Hills Superintendent of Police Vivek Syiem confirmed.
The cause of the fire is yet to be ascertained.
The extent of the damage and the estimated loss are yet to be determined, officials said.

items.title: AU signs MoU with Boston Architectural College
points: Andhra University (AU) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Boston Architectural College (BAC), United States, to expand international academic collaborations and research initiatives.
The agreement was signed in the presence of AU Vice-Chancellor G.P.
Raja Sekhar and BAC President Mahesh Daas.
It provides for dual-degree programmes, postgraduate admissions and joint academic initiatives in architecture, interior architecture, landscape architecture and design studies.
The two institutions will also collaborate in urban design, construction robotics and real estate development, besides facilitating faculty exchanges.
Founded in 1889, BAC is a design institution based in Boston, Massachusetts.

AU officials said the partnership, coinciding with the university’s centenary year, would provide students and faculty members access to global research networks and emerging opportunities in the built environment sector.

Harbour Assembly constituency in Chennai district has the lowest electorate, with 1,20,852 voters (60,043 men, 60,747 women and 62 third-gender electors).

items.title: Sonam Wangchuk Claims "House Arrest" Amid Planned Ladakh Protest
points: A day after police removed Sonam Wangchuk from the protest site and escorted him to his residence, the climate activist on Thursday claimed that he had been placed under house arrest and alleged that around 20–25 police and paramilitary personnel had been…

In a video message shared on his social media accounts, including X and Facebook, late Thursday night, the activist said several security personnel, along with multiple vehicles and tents, had been stationed outside his residence since Wednesday night.
He also alleged that armed personnel were deployed on all sides of his house during the day, restricting his movement.

Referring to the authorities' reported claim that he had merely been "advised to stay at home", Wangchuk questioned the distinction, saying the heavy security deployment effectively amounted to house arrest.

items.title: Women in tech meet discusses operational hurdles in entrepreneurship
points: Organised ahead of the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit, scheduled for November 17 to 19, the event was themed ‘Enabling Women in Tech in Karnataka: From Policy Intent to Action’.
Manjula, Secretary, Department of Electronics, IT & Biotechnology, alongside Sanjeev Kumar Gupta, CEO, Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM).

These included securing early-stage capital for DeepTech and biotechnology ventures, accessing affordable computing power for artificial intelligence firms, expanding market reach, and navigating government procurement processes.
Karnataka currently hosts approximately 8,000 women-led start-ups.

Officials highlighted existing State initiatives, including Women@Work, WEscalate, BioWise, and ELEVATE Shakti, which have committed ₹118.98 crore to over 400 women-led ventures since 2017, including ₹23.19 crore for 63 start-ups in 2026.
To address the specific challenges, the department agreed to explore subsidised AI computing access through the proposed AI Hub and shared facilities for hardware and robotics start-ups.
Ms. Manjula also encouraged founders to utilise the ‘Government First’ initiative, which provides up to ₹25 lakh in pilot support for validating solutions within State departments.

items.title: In Book Scam Order, Madras High Court Judge's Praise For PM's 'Mann Ki Baat'
points: The observation was made by Justice G R Swaminathan in his portion of an order passed by a Division Bench, also comprising Justice M D Sumathi, at the court's Madurai Bench on November 11.

Introducing the observation as a "lighter remark", Justice Swaminathan referred to Mann Ki Baat and wrote: "Thanks to the Hon'ble Prime Minister, we have come to know the great deeds done by several persons in the remote corners of the nation..." He added…
While the remark stood apart from the core issue before the court-alleged irregularities in procuring books for public libraries-the judge explicitly framed the reference as a "lighter remark".

In the same order, Justice Swaminathan recorded that an expert committee member had informed the court that Manathin Kural, the Tamil translation of Mann Ki Baat, had been recommended for procurement but was rejected, failing to reach public library shelves.

items.title: Kalshi ends Donald Trump Jr's advisory contract due to Polymarket conflict
points: Prediction-market platform Kalshi has ended Donald Trump Jr. ’s advisory role by mutual agreement after his venture-capital firm, 1789 Capital, increased its investment in rival Polymarket.
Discussions began after 1789 Capital led Polymarket’s latest funding round, according to a Kalshi spokesperson.

items.title: Chief Of Congress-Allied Kerala Group Arrested In Extortion Case
points: The Kerala Police have arrested the national president of the Congress-allied Kerala Pravasi Association for his alleged involvement in an extortion racket that used forged Enforcement Directorate (ED) notices to target institutions.

Rajendran Vellappalath, who heads the Kerala Pravasi Association-an ally of the United Democratic Front (UDF)-was intercepted and arrested by a Special Investigation Team (SIT) from Nedumbassery in Ernakulam.
The racket came to light during an investigation into an extortion attempt targeting the Indian Cooperative Credit Society Limited (ICCSL), which operates across five states.
The case was set in motion by a formal complaint lodged by Meenu John, Chief Executive Officer of the ICCSL, headquartered at East Fort in Thrissur.
According to the FIR, they received a communication on October 13, which was dated October 5, purportedly issued by the Enforcement Directorate's Delhi Zonal Office-II.
Following the verification, ICCSL CEO Meenu John approached the police and filed a complaint on November 2.

items.title: Rail Vikas Nigam in focus today after mixed Q2 performance; stock down 68% from record peak
points: Shares of Rail Vikas Nigam (RVNL) are expected to attract investor interest during Friday's trade, November 13, after the railway major reported its financial performance for the September quarter (Q2 FY27) post-market hours on Thursday.
The company reported a net profit of ₹253.71 crore in Q2 FY27, registering a growth of 10% year-on-year (YoY) compared to ₹230.52 crore in Q2 FY26.
Revenue from operations declined by 8.24% YoY to ₹4,701 crore in Q2 FY27 from ₹5,123 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.

On the operating front, RVNL reported an operating profit of ₹264 crore in Q2 FY27, marking an increase of 19.51% compared to ₹221 crore in Q2 FY26, indicating an improvement in operating performance despite the decline in revenue.
However, revenue from operations remained almost flat during the six-month period at ₹9,022 crore in H1 FY27 against ₹9,032 crore in H1 FY26, registering a marginal decline of 0.11% YoY.
This came after the stock ended 2025 with a decline of 15.5%.

items.title: Analysis-From SpaceX to Anthropic, markets have a new playbook for mega-share debuts
points: LONDON, Nov 12 (Reuters) - When AI firm Anthropic starts trading after its expected IPO next week, its share price in the first few weeks will largely be determined by who is forced to buy it rather than who wants to buy it.

Elon Musk's SpaceX altered the playbook for stock-market listing by behemoths, as major US index providers such as Nasdaq rewrote the rules around inclusion, ensuring a massive pool of passive money would buy the shares in the first 15 days of its listing.
The Claude chatbot creator aims to raise up to $64.4 billion by selling 825 million shares priced between $70 and $78 each, valuing the firm at up to $1.4 trillion.
Like SpaceX, Anthropic will be added to at least six big indexes, including FTSE's USA index, the S&P Total Market Index and the Nasdaq 100, within 5 to 15 days of its listing.

A case challenging the decision was subsequently filed before the Kerala High Court, he said.
“The State Excise and Taxes departments wrote to the Union Tourism Ministry seeking details of how many applications were pending and how many had been rejected.

items.title: In Manipur, Woman Shot Dead, Two Men Injured In Firing At Taphou Village In Kangpokpi
points: A 40-year-old woman was shot dead and two men sustained bullet injuries in a broad-daylight firing incident at Taphou Kuki village in Kangpokpi district on Thursday, while fresh gunfire was also reported from the Sinakeithei area.
According to a police report, the shooting at Taphou occurred at approximately 11 am.
The two injured men were identified as Sehngam Chongloi alias David, 34, and Lamkhochon Chongloi, both residents of Taphou village.
Sehngam Chongloi was brought to the Regional Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS), Imphal, around 3 pm for further treatment.
Villagers of Taphou reportedly alerted travellers to avoid the affected stretch of National Highway 2 (NH-2).

The Committee on Tribal Unity (CoTU), Sadar Hills, strongly condemned the attack and blamed what it described as the government's persistent inaction and indecision against armed groups, particularly the Tangkhul-led NSCN-IM and ZUF-K.
In a statement issued from Kangpokpi on Thursday, she described the incident as the brutal murder of a defenceless Kuki-Zo woman who was harvesting paddy near Taphou Kuki village.

items.title: Nvidia options traders bank on longer-term stock recovery
points: NEW YORK, - Options traders cashed in parts of their bets against Nvidia and positioned for a longer-term share price recovery on Thursday, after CEO Jensen Huang announced he was stepping down.
The leadership turmoil sent options volatility soaring on Thursday, but options trading suggested that investors were repositioning for a recovery rather than fleeing the stock.

Several large options trades showed investors rolling bullish positions further into 2027, lowering upside targets and taking profits on downside hedges rather than abandoning exposure to the company altogether, data from Chris Murphy, co-head of…
In one trade, an investor sold put options and bought cheaper ones, collecting about $18.9 million while keeping some protection against a further drop, Murphy said.
Another investor paid about $18.8 million for call spreads, a bet that pays off fully if Nvidia climbs about 16% from current levels by March.
Investors also bought about 50,000 January call options, spending an estimated $45.3 million to $55 million to bet the shares will rise above current levels by expiry.

items.title: Seanergy lines up four more bulkers in $855m fleet push
points: Greek capesize specialist Seanergy Maritime has added four more vessels worth $264m to its fleet investment programme, taking its total spending commitments to $855m.

The Nasdaq-listed owner, led by Stamatis Tsantanis, disclosed the latest acquisitions in its third-quarter update, with the deals covering two newbuildings and two secondhand bulkers, for arrivals between 2027 and 2029.
The secondhand purchases comprise a 2019-built Japanese capesize of 180,000 dwt, to be renamed Midnightship, and a 2014-built Japanese newcastlemax of 210,000 dwt.

On the newbuilding side, Seanergy has contracted a scrubber-fitted 210,000 dwt newcastlemax at China’s Hengli Shipbuilding and secured a scrubber-fitted 181,000 dwt capesize under construction in Japan.
The latest additions expand Seanergy’s investment programme to 12 vessels — nine newbuildings and three secondhand ships — representing around 2.3m dwt of additional capacity.
Seanergy has also agreed the main terms of a $33m sale of the 2009-built capesize Friendship to spinoff United Maritime.
Seanergy said it expects to release about $19.6m in net cash and record an accounting gain of $12.4m if completed.

items.title: Tanker Ablaze Off UAE as More Attacks Rattle Gulf Shipping
points: Vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, July 31, 2026.

REUTERS/Stringer A projectile struck the engine room of the Liberia-flagged crude oil tanker Dominica Prosperity off the United Arab Emirates on Wednesday, forcing the evacuation of all 22 crew members as emergency crews battled a fire aboard the vessel.

According to UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), the Dominica Prosperity was struck by an unidentified projectile at approximately 1800 UTC on November 11, about 14 nautical miles northwest of Ras Al Khaimah, UAE, near Mina Saqr.

India’s Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, identified the vessel as the Dominica Prosperity and confirmed that 19 Indian nationals were among the 22 crew members rescued by the UAE Coast Guard.

In its November 12 advisory update, the Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) documented four tanker attacks since its previous report, including two in the Persian Gulf and two in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Central team to visit districts affected by Murasu cyclone

On Friday, the first team will visit Bapatla district, while the second team will tour Eluru district.

items.title: Assam Draft Electoral Roll Has 2.19 Lakh More Voters Than February List
points: The draft roll puts Assam's total electorate at 2,51,76,910.
Of these, 1,25,87,650 are male voters, 1,25,88,939 are female voters, and 321 belong to the third-gender category.
The latest list includes 2,05,962 voters with disabilities, while 2,87,233 electors are in the 18-19 age group.
The number of voters aged 85 years and above stands at 1,22,198.
Assam also has 63,237 service voters and six overseas electors.
Among the Assembly constituencies, Dalgaon has the largest electorate with 3,25,746 voters, while Amri (reserved for ST category) has the smallest, at 1,01,509.

items.title: Vijay Government Hits Six-Month Mark, MLA Says Ready For Trust Vote To Prove Numbers
points: Six months after the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government assumed office in Tamil Nadu, the ruling party is defending its record amid questions over law and order and allegations of misconduct involving two of its legislators.

In an exclusive interview with NDTV, TVK MLA Rhevanth Charan described the government's performance as positive and said it's ready to even face a no-confidence motion, expressing trust in alliance partners.
Rhevanth Charan's assertion comes against the backdrop of the government's dependence on its allies for legislative strength.
TVK has 109 MLAs in the 234-member Tamil Nadu Assembly, against the majority mark of 118.

The government has faced criticism over allegations involving Assembly Deputy Speaker and Thuraiyur MLA Ravi Shankar, who was accused of assaulting a resident, and Kallakurichi MLA Arul Vignesh, who was accused of sending inappropriate WhatsApp messages to…
He said Chief Minister Vijay would look into both incidents and take action against anyone found guilty.

items.title: India records 38% drop in TB mortality since 2015: WHO report
points: Last year, the South-East Asia Region recorded the largest number of new TB cases (35%), followed by the Western Pacific Region (27%) and the African Region (25%).
Around 88% of new TB cases occurred in 30 countries.

India (about a quarter), Indonesia (10%), the Philippines (6.8%), China (6.5%), Pakistan (6.4%), Nigeria (4.9%), the Democratic Republic of the Congo (3.9%) and Bangladesh (3.7%) accounted for about a q of the global total.

Globally, about 50% of people treated for TB and their households face total costs (direct medical expenditures, non-medical expenditures, and indirect costs such as income losses) that are catastrophic (greater than 20% of total household income).
An estimated 9.6 lakh new TB cases were attributable to undernutrition, 9.2 lakh to diabetes, 7.3 lakh to alcohol use disorders, 6.9 lakh to smoking and 5.5 lakh to HIV infection.
The report showed a total of 1.13 million people died from TB in 2025.
Global efforts to combat TB have saved an estimated 86 million lives since 2000.

items.title: Xbox Playback Brings Back Year in Review with a Look at Your Entire Gaming Journey
points: Xbox is celebrating its 25th anniversary with Xbox Playback, a Spotify Wrapped-style recap that brings its traditional Year in Review to mobile, desktop, and, for the first time, Xbox Series X|S consoles.
Alongside the Xbox Game Pass 25th anniversary discount, the recap lets players revisit their entire gaming history, starting with their first milestone.

The Xbox Playback recap will also highlight the device you used to play your favourite Xbox games, your preferred game genres, your total Gamerscore, and your leaderboard ranking based on total hours played across your consoles.
However, Xbox Mythic Achievements aren’t part of the recap.
With Xbox Playback now announced, next year’s recap could be even bigger for Xbox players, with GTA 6 launching next week and likely driving hours of gameplay through the roof.
Sagnik Adhikary is a Gaming News Writer at Beebom with over 4 years of experience covering all sorts of news, guides, listicles, and more.

items.title: CPI(M) seeks withdrawal of proposed Water Regulatory Commission
points: Srinivasa Rao, in a press release, alleged that the government was planning to introduce the commission immediately after the local body elections, contrary to public opinion.

He said the Electricity Regulatory Commission had failed to protect consumers and instead provided cover for successive increases in power tariffs, approval of questionable power purchase agreements and additional true-up charges.
The proposed water regulator would turn drinking and irrigation water into a commercial commodity, allowing private and multinational companies to gain control over rivers and reservoirs, he alleged.

Mr. Srinivasa Rao said the World Bank and the Union government had been pressuring Andhra Pradesh for several years to introduce reforms in the water sector, but successive governments had hesitated due to strong opposition from farmers.
He also criticised the State government's G.O.
160, issued during the local body election period, proposing meters for rural drinking water schemes and collection of user charges based on consumption.

points: Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal shares a light moment with Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N.
Chandrababu Naidu during the inaugural session of the 31st CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam on November 12, 2026. | Photo Credit: K.
The ongoing conflicts cast their shadow on international trade, but India was an exception, with its stable policies and governance that would never let the investors down, he asserted.

Participating as the chief guest in the inaugural session of the 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 in Visakhapatnam on Thursday (November 12, 2026), Mr. Goyal said the world was witnessing multiple crises, challenges and intense competition, but India was…
He recalled that centuries ago, Kakatiya ruler Ganapati Deva, who governed the Andhra region, issued inscriptions assuring foreign investors of confidence and security.
Mr. Goyal said India would fully respect and protect Intellectual Property Rights and extend cooperation to innovators and investors.

items.title: PAN Card, Voter ID Alone Cannot Prove Citizenship: Gauhati High Court
points: The Gauhati High Court has upheld a Foreigners Tribunal order declaring a woman from Assam's Darrang district a foreigner.
The woman had entered India after March 25, 1971, the cut-off date under immigration rules.
Dismissing her petition, the court ruled that PAN cards and voter cards alone cannot establish Indian citizenship or prove family relationships.

A division bench of Justices Kalyan Rai Surana and Susmita Phukan Khaund delivered the judgment on November 5 on a petition filed by Kulchan Begum, challenging a 2018 order of the Foreigners Tribunal at Mangaldai.
Following the Supreme Court's decision to strike down the legislation in 2005, the case was transferred to the Foreigners Tribunal system.
Finding no grounds to interfere with the Tribunal's decision, the High Court dismissed the petition and revoked the interim bail granted to Begum on April 18, 2022.
Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has said the government is invoking the Immigrants (Expulsion from Assam) Act, 1950, to facilitate the return of illegal migrants to Bangladesh.

items.title: When the village becomes an art gallery: 26 homes open their doors to creativity
points: From the art exhibition organised by Niracharthu in Enkakkad What if an art gallery had no white walls, no ticket counter and no imposing entrance?
What if, instead, visitors had to walk through a village, step into its homes and discover paintings displayed on verandas and in domestic spaces?
Twenty-six houses in the village have opened their doors to host ‘10.26’ (Paththu irupathaaru), an exhibition that brings together selected works from the 10-year artistic journey of Niracharthu.
Here, the village itself becomes a gallery, and its homes offer an alternative setting for experiencing visual art.
Instead of asking villagers to travel to urban galleries, it brings art to their doorsteps, placing the domestic veranda in the spotlight as a space for artistic engagement.
More than 50 works by 45 artists who have participated in Niracharthu’s art camps are on display.
By turning familiar homes into exhibition spaces, ‘10.26’ also creates an opportunity for residents to engage with artworks in an informal setting.
The exhibition will continue until December 6.

items.title: Ladakh civil society group begins protest over Home Ministry failure to hold talks
points: Voters queue up outside a polling booth to cast their votes during the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council Election, at Kaksar village in Kargil.
It is the same site where a major demonstration broke out in September 2025.
“Our indefinite dharna is over the MHA’s failure to resume talks with Ladakh groups and holding of hill council elections at the peak of winter.
Already 25% of the population has left Ladakh.
The State Election Commission (SEC) in Ladakh has announced panchayat and municipal elections on November 21 and hill council elections in eight districts on December 4.
“It is sad Mr. Wangchuk, who is an important member of the LAB, was placed under house arrest on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

Meanwhile, BJP leader and ex-Member of Parliament Thupstan Chhewang extended support to the upcoming elections and appealed to the people of Ladakh “to participate wholeheartedly and peacefully in the forthcoming December 4 hill council elections”.

items.title: Third edition of Asian Stroke Summer School begins in Thiruvananthapuram
points: Updated - November 12, 2026 11:04 pm IST - Thiruvananthapuram The third edition of Asian Stroke Summer School 2026, dedicated to advancing comprehensive stroke care across Asia through structured, team-based education and focused hands-on skill…
The programme is organised jointly by Sree Chitra Tirunal Institute for Medical Sciences and Technology (SCTIMST), Thiruvananthapuram and University of Bern, Switzerland.

Modelled on the successful European Stroke Winter School, the Asian Stroke Summer School provides an integrated training platform where neurologists and interventionalists train together as cohesive stroke teams.
The teaching course aims to equip neurologists with updated scientific knowledge so that stroke management can be improved within institutions.
All aspects of stroke management, including clinical decision-making, procedural strategies, complication management and quality of care will be taken up in sessions.

A defining feature of the summer school is its structured hands-on training in stroke intervention using high-fidelity endovascular simulators and silicone vascular flow models The course is led by P.N.
Sylaja, Professor and Head of Comprehensive Stroke Care Programme and E.R.

items.title: TIMS hospitals will be fully operational by June 2, says Chief Minister
points: Revanth Reddy and Health Minister Damodar Rajanarsimha at a meeting in Hyderabad on Thursday.

Revanth Reddy has directed officials to ensure that the TIMS hospitals at Alwal and LB Nagar, Warangal Super Speciality Hospital and the expansion works at NIMS are completed by June 2 next year and made fully operational.
He also set December 2027 as the deadline for completing the construction of the new Osmania General Hospital and making it available to the public.

At a review meeting on the Medical and Health Department on Thursday, the Chief Minister called for a unified recruitment policy for the three TIMS hospitals at Sanathnagar, Alwal and LB Nagar, enabling doctors and other personnel to be transferred between…

The Chief Minister directed officials to make full use of the Sanathnagar TIMS hospital to ease the workload at NIMS, particularly when beds were unavailable or surgeries were getting delayed at the latter institution.

items.title: Nvidia stock crash: Short seller flagged Jensen Huang’s close ties to Alice Huang months before CEO’s resignation
points: The May 13 report by Culper Research, titled The China Problem, questioned Jensen Huang’s association with Alice and examined Megaspeed’s role in the movement of Nvidia-powered servers through Southeast Asia.

It highlighted photographs of the two together at public events in Taiwan in 2024 and 2025 and cited a current Megaspeed employee describing the company’s relationship with the Nvidia chief as “very close”.
The controversy culminated on Thursday, November 12, when Nvidia announced that Huang had resigned as president, CEO and a member of its board, effective immediately.

The stock fell sharply during the week and was down as much as 20% at Thursday’s low, wiping billions of dollars off the chipmaker’s market value and adding to concerns about the fallout from the leadership crisis.
Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is unrelated to Jensen Huang.

items.title: Wind-Powered Cargo Ship Neoliner Origin Cuts Fuel Consumption 70% in First Year
points: French shipping company Neoline says its wind-powered cargo vessel Neoliner Origin has delivered fuel savings of up to 70% during its first year of commercial service, offering an early test of whether wind propulsion can deliver substantial emissions…

The 136-meter roll-on/roll-off cargo ship, which entered service in October 2025, completed nine commercial round trips between Europe and North America, covering more than 62,000 nautical miles and carrying over 12,000 tonnes of cargo.

According to first-year operating results released by Neoline, the vessel reduced fuel consumption by an average of 66% over its first year compared with conventional vessels using the Global Logistics Emissions Council (GLEC) fleet reference.
Savings reached 70% when considering 2026 operations alone.

The Return of Sail Power: Cargo Ships Are Turning Back to the Wind A separate analysis comparing Neoliner Origin with a simulated conventional vessel operating the same routes at 15 knots found fuel savings ranging from 62% to 67%, although Neoline…

items.title: 3 Minors Among 4 Killed In Massive Fire In Arunachal's Kurung Kumey
points: A massive fire broke out in Arunachal Pradesh's Kurung Kumey district at around 2 am on Thursday, killing four people including three minors, said officials.
The incident happened in Kurung Kumey's Parsi Parlo town.
All four victims were from the same family, said Parsi Parlo's Additional DC Nabam Tajik.
Around 30 shops and houses were destroyed in the fire, which engulfed the entire area within a short period of time.
Parsi Parlo does not have any fire station or fire tenders.
The nearest fire station is at Koloriang, the district headquarters of Kurung Kumey district, which is over four-hour drive away from Parsi Parlo.
Police have launched an investigation into what caused the fire.
Chief Minister Pema Khandu expressed condolences over the tragic incident.

items.title: Kerala High Court says it may order medical board examination to verify Tomin Thachankary’s illnesses
points: A medical examination may be required to verify former DGP Tomin Thachankary’s illnesses as he did not spend a day in a jail cell during his incarceration in the disproportionate assets case, the Kerala High Court has remarked.
Badharudeen was on Thursday considering a plea by Thachankary seeking a modification of his bail conditions to travel abroad and resume his employment in the United Arab Emirates.
“We need to know whether it was an illness or a conspiracy to avoid staying in a cell,” the court orally observed.

Thachankary had sought permission to withdraw his plea; however, the court noted that there was an anomaly in the contentions raised by the petitioner and remarked that the matter required serious consideration.
“He (Thachankary) might have visited a prison cell while he was serving as police chief, but not during his sentence,” the court said.
The Poojappura Central Jail superintendent had previously produced Thachankary’s medical records.

items.title: Police bust interstate vape supply network in Hyderabad, man arrested
points: A 28-year-old man was arrested for selling banned e-cigarettes and foreign cigarettes through an outlet in Raidurgam, with investigators suspecting that the shop was part of a wider interstate supply network involving online orders and doorstep deliveries.
The accused has been identified as Aboobacker Siddique, a native of Kerala, who worked as the manager of Smokin Spot in Raidurgam and was staying at a private hostel in Madhapur.
Police seized 46 e-cigarettes, 49 packets of foreign cigarettes, two mobile phones and two digital payment scanners from the outlet.
The owner, Mohammed Shareef, and a suspected supplier, Arshad, both natives of Kerala, are being traced.
According to investigators, Shareef appointed Siddique as the manager in March 2026 on a monthly salary of ₹25,000.
Nihad Ahmed, a native of Karnataka, had been working at the outlet and allegedly trained Siddique before leaving after about a month.
The outlet reportedly sold around 107 e-cigarettes during October and November, at prices ranging from ₹2,800 to ₹4,000 depending on their puff capacity.

items.title: Parts of former TMC strongman Jahangir Khan's house demolished
points: The South 24 Parganas district administration has demolished an unauthorised portion of a home belonging to former Trinamool Congress strongman Jahangir Khan in Falta.
Mr. Jahangir was arrested on July 8 from the India-Nepal border for extortion, murder, and criminal intimidation.
The operation began around 8.30 a.m. under BDO Sandip Singh Roy, with fire department personnel and a large police contingent deployed to maintain law and order.
According to the police, several notices were issued to Mr. Jahangir to remove the structure.
The building exceeded two storeys and lacked approval.
Mr. Jahangir was the TMC’s candidate in the Falta Assembly constituency and dropped out of the race just ahead of the repoll.
Following his arrest, Mr. Khan’s office in Falta was reportedly vandalised.

items.title: Finland Says it Detects Strike on Russian Warship in Baltic Sea
points: Russian Navy Steregushchy-class corvette Boikiy sails under the Great Belt bridge towards the Baltic Sea, in Korsor, Denmark, January 24, 2026.

REUTERS/Yoruk Isik HELSINKI, Nov 12 (Reuters) – Finland’s military said on Thursday its forces had detected “a strike” on a Russian warship in the Baltic Sea a day earlier, but that the security situation in the area remained stable.

“The Finnish Defence Forces detected… a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland area and has monitored the development of the situation,” a spokesperson for the Nordic country’s military said in an emailed statement to Reuters.
Some Ukrainian drones have strayed into the airspace of Finland and the Baltic region, leading to fears that the war is spilling over into NATO countries that border Russia and its ally Belarus.
The Gulf of Finland is a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea between Finland and Estonia that extends eastwards to St Petersburg.

items.title: Siddhasiri cooperative society urges people not to panic following reports over its financial health
points: MLA Basanagouda Patil Yatnal is the head of the Multi-State, Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society. | Photo Credit: FILE PHOTO Siddhasiri Multi-State, Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society has urged the public not to panic about news reports of the Union…
The Vijayapura-based cooperative is headed by MLA Basanagouda Patil Yatnal.
Legal advisor for the society Satish Chandra Kulkarni told reporters in Vijayapura on Thursday that there is absolutely no problem with the financial health of the institution.
“Reports of a raid on the society are false and baseless.
We have only received a notice from the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies seeking some clarifications.
A team of officials, including joint managing director and internal auditor of the society, went to New Delhi and answered all their questions and clarified doubts.
We have given appropriate answers to all the 11 questions raised by the Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies.

items.title: Hyderabad Police launch AI platform to map accused persons and criminal networks
points: Investigating officers in Hyderabad can now use an artificial intelligence-based platform to analyse the activities, backgrounds and criminal networks of accused persons, with the city police launching an in-house system aimed at reducing the time spent…
Named Dooradrishti, the crime intelligence and investigation support platform was launched by Hyderabad Police Commissioner V.C.
Sajjanar at the Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) on Thursday.
The platform is designed to provide investigating officers with a consolidated picture of an accused person and help them identify links with other individuals and criminal networks.
Police said the information previously required days of manual work across different records and databases, while the new system would bring the data together on a single platform.

Speaking at the launch, Sajjanar said Dooradrishti was developed by Hyderabad City Police personnel and would put years of police data to use in speeding up investigations and helping victims get quicker justice.

items.title: Kharagpur becomes first IIT to offer PG medical programmes
points: Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur.

File | Photo Credit: The Hindu Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur has become the first IIT in India to offer postgraduate medical degree programmes accredited by the National Medical Commission (NMC).
Starting in the 2026–27 academic year, the institute will welcome its first cohort of MD students at the Dr. B.
Roy Multi-Speciality Medical Research Centre.
Six specialisations will be offered: General Medicine, Radiology, Physiology, Pathology, Community Medicine, and Biochemistry, with two seats available in each discipline.
The move marks a significant shift by introducing specialist medical training into an IIT ecosystem, opening opportunities for collaboration between doctors, engineers, and researchers.
IIT Kharagpur’s expertise in artificial intelligence, computational sciences, microfluidics, bioengineering, and healthcare diagnostics is expected to support this interdisciplinary approach.

Admissions for the 2026–27 academic year will be conducted through the NEET-PG online counselling process, with the programmes listed under Round 2 in line with the official schedule, eligibility criteria, and seat matrix.

items.title: Vettucaud Church feast in Keralam to get under way on November 13
points: The Pontifical Holy Mass will be led by Auxiliary Bishop R.
Christudas of the Latin Archdiocese of Thiruvananthapuram at 4.30 p.m., followed by the hoisting of the ceremonial flag.
A procession carrying the statue of Christ the King will be taken out in connection with the festival.

items.title: Supriya Sule rules out NCP merger talks, says ‘no one has approached me’
points: Sule said she had neither received any merger proposal nor been approached by anyone on the matter.
Her remarks came shortly after Maharashtra NCP president Sunil Tatkare said he saw no substance in the speculation surrounding merger talks between the two factions.

Sule, who was in New Delhi, chose to break her silence on the speculation nearly two weeks after it gained momentum following a meeting between six senior NCP leaders and Union home minister Amit Shah on November 1.

From my side, the matter ended there.” For the unversed, Ajit Pawar, nephew of Sharad Pawar, had split the NCP in July 2023 and subsequently secured the party's original name and election symbol after joining the ruling Mahayuti alliance in Maharashtra.
However, less than three years after the split, the two factions began exploring the possibility of reunification, with Ajit Pawar keen to bring the parties together by February 12.

items.title: ABS and Radian Forge Collaborate on Digital Qualification for Additive Manufacturing
points: ABS and Radian Forge have signed a joint development project (JDP) to evaluate the use of digital manufacturing data in the qualification of metal components produced through wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM).

As the maritime industry explores additive manufacturing to address component availability and long production lead times, confidence in the consistency and performance of manufactured parts is critical.
“Digital qualification has an important role to play in the adoption of additive manufacturing across the marine and offshore sectors.

We are proud to work with Radian Forge to strengthen confidence in additive manufacturing by improving how qualification evidence is generated, evaluated and traced,” said Michael Kei, ABS Vice President, Technology.
Under the agreement, Radian Forge will manufacture components for testing and validation, collect manufacturing and sensor data, and conduct applicable testing.
Partnering with ABS gives us an opportunity to rigorously evaluate how process data and material performance can support that objective,” said Jeff Yeager, CEO of Radian Forge.

points: The yatra is part of the Congress's political mobilisation ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections.
The eight-day yatra, running from November 12 to 19, will cover nearly 625 km across at least 27 of the 117 Assembly constituencies.

The 'Jawani Sambhal Cycle Yatra' was flagged off by @SachinPilot ji. @RahulGandhi @kharge @INCIndia https://t.co/PhQCkwSP5W Reacting to the rally, Mann challenged the former chief minister to distribute the 2,000 bicycles used in the yatra among the poor…

items.title: Paytm shares at ₹1,925, close in on IPO listing-day high after 100% rally from March lows. What drove the recovery?
points: The shares ended today's session 7.3% higher at ₹1,925, their highest closing level since making their stock market debut in November 2021.
Paytm shares closed higher in five of the seven months since then, with a 28% return in August marking their biggest-ever monthly gain and has rebounded 100% from March lows.
At the end of the September quarter, 43 mutual funds collectively held a 21.17% stake in Paytm, equivalent to approximately 13.5 crore shares.
This marked a notable increase from the 17.94% stake held at the end of the previous quarter in June, according to Trendlyne's shareholding data.
The journey of One 97 Communications, Paytm's parent company, since its ₹18,300-crore IPO has been marked by sharp twists and turns following the fintech major's listing in November 2021.

Laurus Labs, Gland Pharma, Piramal Pharma, and Divi’s Laboratories are some of the key pharma stocks in the space which have delivered up to 90% return over the past six months.

items.title: KTM 1390 Super Duke GT Evo Revealed With 187 HP V-Twin Engine And AMT Gearbox
points: KTM has revealed the 1390 Super Duke GT Evo at EICMA 2026, giving its flagship sports tourer an automated manual gearbox and upgraded suspension.
The Evo sits above the standard 1390 Super Duke GT and combines superbike-level performance with the equipment needed to cover long distances.
KTM says the new range will reach international dealerships in early 2027.
The gearbox comes alongside a 1,350cc V-twin producing 187hp and 145Nm, so this is hardly a relaxed touring motorcycle with a token sporting badge.
The liquid-cooled, 75-degree LC8 V-twin is closely related to the engine used in KTM's 1390 Super Adventure S Evo.
It produces 187hp and 145Nm of torque, figures that put the GT Evo firmly in the high-performance end of the sports-touring market.
At the front is a 48mm upside-down fork with KTM's thru-rod design; at the rear is a linked monoshock.
Braking hardware is equally serious: twin 320mm front discs with Brembo Stylema four-piston monoblock callipers and a 240mm rear disc.

items.title: Muthoot FinCorp diversifies funding to trim borrowing cost
points: The Kerala-based non-banking financial company (NBFC) plans to raise up to ₹3,000 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares The gold loan-focused NBFC strengthened access to overseas borrowings and debt capital markets, bringing down its cost of funds,…

IPO-bound Muthoot FinCorp has reduced its average cost of borrowing by 121 basis points to 9.11 per cent in FY26 from 10.32 per cent in FY25, supported by a diversified funding mix and increased access to overseas borrowings and debt capital markets.

The Kerala-based non-banking financial company (NBFC) plans to raise up to ₹3,000 crore through a fresh issue of equity shares, with the proceeds intended to strengthen its tier-I capital base and support future lending requirements.
Overseas borrowings accounted for 9.20 per cent of Muthoot FinCorp’s total borrowings in March 2026, compared with 1.65 per cent in March 2024.
Commercial paper, which was introduced into its funding mix during this period, accounted for 8.92 per cent of total borrowings by March 2026.

items.title: Global TB Report 2026: Nearly 10.6 million fell ill with TB worldwide; India accounts for 25% of cases
points: An estimated 10.6 million people fell ill with tuberculosis (TB) worldwide in 2025, a decline of 75,000 from the previous year, while India continued to account for about a quarter of the global disease burden, according to the World Health Organization’s…
The report also noted a 38% reduction in TB deaths in India since 2015, compared with a 35% decline globally.
The global TB, the report added, incidence rate declined by 1.6% between 2024 and 2025, from 131 to 129 cases per one lakh people.

However, the reduction remains far below the World Health Organization’s End TB Strategy milestones, which called for a 50% decline in TB incidence by 2025 and an 80% reduction by 2030, compared with 2015 levels.
Between 2015 and 2025, the global incidence rate fell by 14%.
The 30 countries with a high TB burden accounted for 88% of the estimated global cases in 2025.

items.title: Raghav Chadha Celebrates His Birthday With Prayers At Gurdwara
points: Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha marked his 38th birthday on Wednesday by offering prayers and performing 'sewa' at a gurdwara.
During his visit, Chadha paid obeisance before Sri Guru Granth Sahib, received a siropa from the gurdwara, and offered prayers at the Nishan Sahib.
Sharing moments from the visit on Instagram, he said, "Sewa at the Guru's house brings a peace that nothing else can.

The only feeling in my heart at the Guru's house was "shukrana" (gratitude), adding that through Waheguru Ji's mehar (grace), I have received a lot in life, and considers it all his bakhshish (blessing)." Chadha participated in several sewa activities.
He also interacted with members of the sangat, including families and children who had gathered at the gurdwara.
Chadha concluded his visit with a prayer for continued blessings upon everyone, wishing all "Chardi Kala", a spirit of eternal optimism, strength and positivity.

items.title: US set to host Quad Leaders Summit in Manila next week
points: Quad member states are expected to unveil several deliverables, mainly focused on economic security and strategic infrastructure, at the leaders’ summit that is expected to be held on the margins of the Asean Summit in Manila next week, people familiar…

The upcoming Quad Leaders’ Summit — the first gathering of the leaders of India, Australia, Japan and the US since September 2024 — is set to be hosted by the US, the people said on condition of anonymity.
India was set to chair the leaders’ summit in 2025, but its efforts to arrange the meeting last year were hampered by a lack of clarity over US President Donald Trump’s travel plans.

The deliverables expected to be unveiled at the upcoming summit were finalised at the Quad foreign ministers’ meeting on the margins of the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta on October 31, the people said.

items.title: Singapore Retains Crown as World’s Leading Maritime Hub
points: The Leading Maritime Cities 2026 report, released Thursday, ranks Singapore first overall, followed by Shanghai, London, Rotterdam and Tokyo.
Tokyo also returned to the top five, replacing Oslo, which ranked fifth in 2024.
Singapore ranked first in three of the report’s five categories: Shipping, Ports and Logistics, and Attractiveness and Competitiveness.
It also placed third in Maritime Finance and Law and fourth in Maritime Technology.
Houston fell five positions to 20th, while Los Angeles dropped from 19th to 25th.

The changes come as Asian maritime centers gain ground in the rankings, although DNV and Menon Economics caution that methodological updates in the 2026 report may affect comparisons with previous editions.
Asia now holds three of the top five places, up from two in 2024,” said Erik Jakobsen, partner and chair of Menon Economics.

Orders for alternative-fueled ships are running 57% ahead of last year, with LNG-powered containerships and car carriers driving much of the growth, according to new figures from classification society DNV....

items.title: Farewell to America’s Flagship: SS United States Sinks After 74 Years
points: Crews prepare to sink the former ocean liner SS United States to create an artificial reef about 22 miles off the coast of Destin, Florida, US, November 11, 2026.
The legendary ocean liner, which still holds the transatlantic speed record, took hours to sink off Florida’s Gulf Coast, ending a remarkable chapter in American maritime history.

The SS United States, the fastest ocean liner ever built and one of the last great symbols of America’s maritime golden age, sank off Florida’s Gulf Coast Wednesday night, November 11, bringing a 74-year journey to an end.
The 990-foot vessel disappeared beneath the Gulf around 9 p.m.
Central Time, following an hours-long controlled sinking operation approximately 22 nautical miles southwest of Destin-Fort Walton Beach.

The SS United States was the vision of legendary naval architect William Francis Gibbs, who spent much of his career pursuing the dream of building an American ocean liner capable of outperforming Europe’s finest ships.
